h1: The 6 Best TV Stands for Bedroom of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best TV Stand for Bedroom 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six bedroom TV stands, from a 31.7 inch cabinet to a nine-drawer dresser TV stand, with size, storage and budget advice.
summary: The WLIVE 58 inch stand is the best TV stand for a bedroom, a low 18 inch unit rated for TVs from 55 to 65 inches and 110 lb on top. The EnHomee doubles as a dresser with nine fabric drawers and charging, and the smaller WLIVE suits 32 to 40 inch TVs. The Furinno is the lowest at 15 inches, the Prepac has a 5-year warranty, and the Yaheetech adds four outlets but stands 24.5 inches tall.
intro: Bedroom TV stands fail on height, not width. A living-room unit that stands 25 inches tall puts the screen above your sight line once you are propped on pillows, and you end up craning at it. That is why the best bedroom stands run low, roughly 14 to 18 inches, or double as a dresser when floor space is tight.

Our editors compared six stands from their listed dimensions, TV size ranges, weight ratings and storage, and ranked them on the Primea score. Height and weight capacity decided most positions, with storage type and cable handling next. Measure the wall, the TV width and the bed-to-screen distance before you choose, because those three numbers settle half the field, and none of them appears on a product photo.

products.name: WLIVE 58" TV Stand for 65 Inch TVs, Mid Century Modern Entertainment Center
products.verdict: A low 18 inch stand that holds up to a 65 inch TV.
products.description:
The WLIVE 58 inch stand measures 58 by 14.6 by 18 inches, fits TVs from 55 to 65 inches, and holds 110 lb on top and 22 lb on its lower shelf. The doors close quietly on magnets, and cable management is built in, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Quiet doors matter in a bedroom, where a slamming cabinet wakes a partner.

It wins because the 18 inch height keeps the screen near eye level from bed, and the 110 lb top rating covers a 65 inch TV with margin. The EnHomee gives storage but at nearly twice the height.

Buy it for bedrooms with a 55 to 65 inch TV. The caveats are the 22 lb lower shelf limit and no clothes storage. Skip it if you need a dresser in the same footprint.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms with a 55 to 65 inch TV.

products.name: EnHomee 55" Dresser for Bedroom with Charging Station, 65 Inch TV Stand with 9 Fabric Drawers
products.verdict: A TV stand and a dresser in one 55 inch unit.
products.description:
The EnHomee measures 55.12 by 11.81 by 35.43 inches, holds a TV up to 65 inches, and has nine fabric drawers rated 22 lb each. It adds two AC and two USB charging ports, adjustable RGB lighting and anti-tip hardware, in the $50 to $100 bracket. The shallow 11.81 inch depth keeps it from jutting into a small room.

It ranks second because the dresser function is valuable in a small bedroom, but at 35.43 inches tall the screen sits well above bed height. Fabric drawers are also softer than wood.

Buy it for a small bedroom that needs both storage and a screen. The caveats are the tall frame and soft fabric drawers. Skip it if you watch from bed and want the screen low, where the WLIVE or Furinno fit better.
products.idealFor: Small bedrooms needing storage and a screen.
products.skipIf: You watch from bed and want a low screen.

products.name: WLIVE TV Stand for 40 Inch TVs, Small Entertainment Center with Storage Cabinet
products.verdict: A 31.7 inch cabinet for 32 to 40 inch TVs.
products.description:
This WLIVE stand is 31.7 inches wide, 21.9 inches tall and 15.7 inches deep, fits 32 to 40 inch TVs, and has a three-level adjustable shelf plus cable holes. It sits on tapered mid-century legs, in the $50 to $100 bracket. A closed cabinet hides boxes and cords, which tidies a small room.

It ranks third because it is the smallest, which suits guest rooms and dorms, but it handles only a 40 inch TV and stands taller than the 58 inch model. The adjustable shelf helps with game consoles and streaming boxes.

Buy it for a guest room or dorm with a small TV. The caveats are the 40 inch limit and the extra height. Skip it if you own a TV above 40 inches.
products.idealFor: Guest rooms and dorms with a small TV.
products.skipIf: You own a TV above 40 inches.

products.name: Furinno Econ Low Rise TV Stand, Black/Black
products.verdict: A 15 inch tall open stand that keeps the screen low.
products.description:
The Furinno Econ measures 48.7 by 15 by 14.6 inches, holds 60 lb on top, and has stepped three-tier open shelving in FSC-certified composite wood with rounded corners, in the $50 to $100 bracket. At a 15 inch height, it is the lowest stand in this guide, which keeps a screen at bed level.

It ranks fourth because the lowest height is a big plus for bed viewing, but the 60 lb limit is the smallest top rating here and open shelves show clutter. Against the WLIVE 58 inch, it holds less and shows more.

Buy it for bedrooms where the TV sits low and a simple build suffices. The caveats are the 60 lb limit and exposed shelves. Skip it if you prefer closed doors or own a heavy TV.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms where the TV sits low.

products.name: Prepac Essentials TV Stand, Black, 60"
products.verdict: A 60 inch stand with four compartments and a 5-year warranty.
products.description:
The Prepac Essentials is 60 by 19.75 by 15.75 inches with a built-in wire management system and four separate storage compartments. It is CARB-compliant composite wood with a 5-year manufacturer warranty, ready to assemble. A five-year warranty is the longest coverage in this guide.

It ranks fifth because no weight rating is listed, so you cannot check it against your TV, and it stands taller than the WLIVE 58 inch at 19.75 inches. The four compartments and wire management are real conveniences.

Buy it if long warranty coverage matters to you. The caveats are the missing weight limit and the added height. Skip it if you need a stated capacity, and check your TV's weight against the manufacturer before relying on it.
products.skipIf: You need a stated weight limit.

products.name: Yaheetech TV Stand for TV up to 65 inch, Media Entertainment Center with Power Outlets
products.verdict: Four built-in AC outlets on a 55 inch open stand.
products.description:
The Yaheetech is 55 by 24.5 by 16 inches, fits TVs up to 65 inches, and has four AC ports on a 1500W, 2 meter cord, X-shaped side reinforcement and three open tiers. Built-in outlets help rooms with few wall sockets, and reinforcement adds stiffness.

It ranks last because 24.5 inches is the tallest here, which puts the screen well above bed height. The four outlets are handy, but a power strip does the same for a few dollars.

Buy it for rooms short on wall outlets. The caveats are the height and open-only shelving. Skip it if you lie down to watch, because the screen will sit above your line of sight.

whatMatters.detail: Height sets where your screen lands relative to your eyes. In a bedroom you often sit or lie lower than in a living room. Look at the height figure in the listing, and aim for roughly 14 to 25 inches for bed viewing, lower if you watch while lying flat on your back. Sit on the bed and measure your eye height first.

Listings state the TV sizes they support, such as 55 to 65 inches. Putting a bigger TV on a small stand makes it unstable, and a TV with wide feet can overhang the edges. Compare your TV's width and foot spacing to the stand's width before ordering, and leave a few inches each side. A TV that overhangs is a tip hazard.

Top capacity is the maximum weight the surface holds, like 110 lb on the WLIVE 58 inch. Check your TV's weight on its spec sheet and stay under the number. Look for a stated figure, since the Prepac lists none, and remember a lower shelf rating, like 22 lb, applies to consoles.

Closed doors hide clutter, drawers hold clothes and open shelves are faster to reach. The choice depends on what you keep nearby. Check the storage description in the title, and think about whether you need a dresser, since the EnHomee replaces one while most others do not. Fabric drawers hold light clothing, not heavy folded stacks.

Depth is how far the stand sticks out from the wall. In a small bedroom 11 to 16 inches is easier to live with. Look for the D figure in the dimension line, and check the TV's own base depth, which can be larger than a shallow stand and tip forward. Measure the whole footprint, not just the width.

faq.q: What height is best for a bedroom TV stand?
faq.a: Lower is better for bed viewing. The Furinno at 15 inches and the WLIVE at 18 inches suit it, while the Yaheetech at 24.5 inches puts the screen high.

Picking a stand by width and ignoring height. A tall stand like the EnHomee pushes the screen above your eye line when you are lying down, so check the height figure first. A low stand costs the same as a tall one.

faq.q: Is the EnHomee worth it over a plain stand?
faq.a: Yes if you need drawers, since it replaces a dresser and adds charging. Skip it if you watch from bed, because its 35.43 inch height puts the screen high.

faq.q: How do I secure a stand?
faq.a: The EnHomee includes anti-tip hardware. For other stands, add your own anchors per the manual, especially in a room with children or a large TV on the Yaheetech or Prepac. Tipping is the main bedroom hazard.

faq.q: How do I care for the finish?
faq.a: Wipe with a dry or slightly damp cloth and avoid standing water on composite wood. The Furinno and Prepac use composite wood that swells if it gets wet, so wipe spills at once.

faq.q: Can a 65 inch TV fit on a 58 inch stand?
faq.a: The WLIVE 58 inch lists 55 to 65 inch TVs, so yes. Check your TV's feet spacing against the 58 inch width, and keep the top load under 110 lb. A TV on its own legs may be wider than the stand.

finalTake: Choose the WLIVE 58 inch for a bedroom with a 55 to 65 inch TV and no clothes storage need. Take the EnHomee if you lack a dresser and can live with a taller screen. The smaller WLIVE and Furinno suit small rooms and low viewing angles, and the Prepac rewards buyers who want long coverage. Skip the Yaheetech if you watch lying down, because it is the tallest here.
